headline: AI-credit scare deepens overnight, but Friday brings tentative dip-buying
body: The inflation scare that rattled markets Wednesday was compounded Thursday by a hotter-than-expected September PPI print, and the selloff that followed looked less like routine profit-taking and more like a credit-quality scare inside the AI trade: CoreWeave fell roughly 15%, then another 8% the next day, after reports that its 2032 unsecured bonds were trading at distressed-debt yield levels -- bond investors pricing real default risk into AI infrastructure financing, not just equity holders trimming growth multiples. Broadcom's CEO added to the unease, saying financing capacity, not chips or electricity, could be the binding constraint on further AI buildout. The contagion went global: Korea's Kospi dropped roughly 8%, SK Hynix fell about 11%, Japan's Nikkei lost around 5%, and twenty leading AI and semiconductor names reportedly shed over $1 trillion combined this week, even as TSMC posted record quarterly profit the same day.

Friday's premarket tone is notably calmer: S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were fractionally higher (around 0.1-0.15%), Dow futures up roughly 0.2%, and the smaller-cap Russell 2000 outperforming at closer to 0.3%, consistent with money easing back out of the most crowded, capex-heavy AI names rather than abandoning equities outright. Headlines are already framing this as 'AI jitters fading,' though a single calmer premarket session after two sharp down days doesn't yet confirm the rotation is over, especially with Fed officials still weighing a possible October hike after the CPI and PPI surprises. Retail-sentiment chatter was thin and inconclusive in today's searches, so this read leans on price action, credit-market signals, and the macro data rather than social-media positioning.
